summary: parseCompound for ms parses strings like "1h 30m" into total milliseconds, returning NaN on bad input. It is built, committed twice and uses an anchored regex with a length cap. No PR or release is recorded.
narrative: On Nov 2 the owner asked for a separate PR adding parseCompound, with an export from src/index.ts and tests. The agent found that feat/compound already held the formatISO commit, so it cut feat/parse-compound from main (obs 4, 6). parseCompound was added and committed as 7ed8d44 (obs 9, 10). The owner then said to use a single anchored regex for the whole string in the style of parse(), with a capped input length, because the reviewer prefers that. The implementation was reworked to an upfront anchored validation regex plus a matchAll loop and a 100-character limit, committed as 6cc46a1 (obs 11, 12). Memory shows no PR opening, merge, release or owner sign-off, so it is in review-ready state.
